EDP-22.alt: The loop with X and Y a quarter-turn apart: the short arc is 4 ohms carrying 1.8 A, the long arc is 12 ohms carrying 0.6 A, with 7.2 V across the loop.

EDP-25-q.alt: Circuit: a square-wave supply in series with a sealed box between terminals P and Q and a 6.0 ohm resistor, beside a graph of the supply output switching between +12 V and -12 V every 10 ms.

EDP-27-q.alt: Two plane mirrors meeting at O at an angle of 25 degrees, with a beam entering parallel to the lower mirror 30 cm from it.

EDP-27.alt: Unfolded copies of the 25 degree gap around O, with the beam drawn as a straight line 30 cm from O crossing the lines at 25 to 175 degrees seven times.

EE1-7-q.alt: A cumulative frequency polygon for 200 journey times through the points (0,0), (10,24), (15,54), (20,90), (35,150) and (60,200).

EE1-11.alt: A rectangle ABCD with an interior point P joined to all four corners, and dashed lines through P parallel to the sides splitting the distances into p, q, r and s.

EE1-13-q.alt: Distance apart in km against time in minutes, falling in a straight line from 6 at time 0 to 0 at 12 minutes, rising to 4 at 20 minutes, then falling to 3 at 30 minutes.

EE1-14.alt: A square ABCD with an equilateral triangle ABE on top, the circle through C, D and E with centre O, and the equilateral triangle DOC showing that the radius equals the side.

EE1-15-q.alt: The graph of y = f(x) made of line segments joining (-4,-1), (-2,3), (0,1), (1,3), (3,-2) and (4,0) on a unit grid.

EE1-16.alt: A 60 by 60 square of arrival times with the shaded band between the lines b = a + 10 and b = a - 20, and two unshaded corner triangles with legs 50 and 40.

EE1-18.alt: An equiangular hexagon with sides 4, 2, 3, 3, 3, 2 shown as an equilateral triangle of side 8 with three small equilateral triangles of sides 2, 3 and 2 cut from its corners.

EE1-21.alt: The folded rectangle: trapezium AEFD stays in place and the flap folds to the quadrilateral E B' A F, overlapping it in triangle EAF, with the original position of the flap dashed.

EE1-22.alt: The arc of y = 2^x from A(0,1) to B(3,8) and its translate from A'(3,-1) to B'(6,6), with the region between them shaded and the chords AB and A'B' dashed to show the parallelogram.

EE1-27.alt: A row of parabolic arches y = (x - 2m)^2 between odd integers, crossed by the line y = x/5 at x = 0, 0.2, about 1.46, about 2.74, 3.2, and touching the peak at x = 5.

EEP-2-q.alt: Graph of current against p.d. for a thermistor X, a curve bending upwards, and a fixed resistor Y, a straight line through the origin, crossing at P where V is 4 V and I is 0.5 A.

EEP-2.alt: The same current against p.d. graph with the tangent to curve X at P drawn dashed, visibly steeper than the line Y from the origin through P.

EEP-5-q.alt: Graph of time to boil against mass of water: a straight line through crosses at (0.5 kg, 100 s), (1.0 kg, 180 s) and (1.5 kg, 260 s), drawn from 0.25 kg to 1.75 kg.

EEP-5.alt: The kettle graph with the line extended back to an intercept of 20 s at zero mass, and a gradient triangle showing 160 s per 1.0 kg.

EEP-6-q.alt: Cross-section of a canal lock gate standing on the floor, with water 5.0 m deep on the upstream side and 3.0 m deep on the downstream side.

EEP-6.alt: Graph of gauge pressure against depth below the upstream surface: the upstream line rises from 0 to 50 kPa over 5 m, the downstream line from 0 at 2 m to 30 kPa at 5 m, and the shaded gap between them splits into a triangle of area 20 and a band of area 60.

EEP-7-q.alt: A 16 V battery feeding a resistor ladder: four 1 kilohm resistors in series along the top through nodes A, B, C and D, a 2 kilohm resistor from each node down to the return wire, and a final 2 kilohm resistor at the right-hand end.

EEP-7.alt: The ladder circuit annotated with node p.d.s of 8, 4, 2 and 1 V at A to D and currents of 8, 4, 2 and 1 mA in the top resistors, 4, 2, 1 and 0.5 mA in the vertical resistors and 0.5 mA in the end resistor.

EEP-8-q.alt: Table: spring compression 2.0 cm gives greatest height 0.30 m; 4.0 cm gives 1.80 m; 6.0 cm is unknown.

EEP-9-q.alt: Graph of power in the resistor against time from 0 to 40 ms, a smooth wave rising from zero to peaks of 8 W at 5, 15, 25 and 35 ms and falling to zero at 0, 10, 20, 30 and 40 ms.

EEP-10-q.alt: Graph of cord force against distance: a straight line falling from 30 N at 0 m to 0 N at 6 m, then zero up to 10 m.

EEP-10.alt: The cord force graph with a dashed friction line at 10 N; the triangle between the force line and the friction line up to x = 4 m is shaded and labelled 40 J.

EEP-11-q.alt: Upper graph: displacement at the sensor against time, zero until 0.5 s, rising steeply to 4 cm at 1.0 s and falling steadily to zero at 2.0 s. Below, six graphs A to F of displacement against position from 0 to 6 m, each showing a triangular pulse in a different place or orientation.

EEP-11.alt: The rope at t = 2.5 s: zero up to x = 1 m (the tail, which passed the sensor at 2.0 s), rising to a 4 cm peak at x = 3 m (passed at 1.0 s), then dropping steeply to zero at x = 4 m (the front, passed at 0.5 s).

EEP-12-q.alt: Graph of thrust against time: rising linearly from 0 to 8 N over the first 0.5 s, constant at 8 N until 1.5 s, then falling linearly to 0 at 2.0 s.

EEP-12.alt: The thrust graph with a dashed weight line at 4.0 N; lift-off at 0.25 s; the region above the line is shaded as +5.0 N s and the small triangle below it after 1.75 s as -0.5 N s.

EEP-13.alt: Graph of drum p.d. in kilovolts against charge in microcoulombs, a straight line through the origin; the trapezium under it between 1 and 3 microcoulombs, from 10 kV to 30 kV, is shaded and labelled 40 mJ.

EEP-15-q.alt: Cooling curve of temperature against time: liquid wax cools from about 82 degrees C to 55 degrees C by 10 min, stays at 55 degrees C until 40 min, then the solid cools towards 32 degrees C at 55 min; dashed tangents pass through (0, 75) and (15, 45), and through (40, 55) and (50, 30).

EEP-16-q.alt: Perspective sketch of a horizontal rectangular duct 10 cm high and 4.0 cm deep, with a 30 cm section where the magnetic field B points into the page, an electrode on the top wall, a current I flowing downwards, and an arrow showing the flow to the right.

EEP-17-q.alt: Temperature against distance through a wall: a steep straight line falls from 20 degrees C to 4 degrees C across a 5 cm insulating board, then a shallow line falls from 4 degrees C to 0 degrees C across 20 cm of brick.

EEP-18.alt: Two circuits: in experiment 1 resistors R1 and R2 are in series from X through Y to Z across 230 V; in experiment 2 X and Z are joined so that R1 and R2 are in parallel between XZ and Y across 230 V.

EEP-20-q.alt: Graph of spring extension against time: rising from 0 to 5 mm over 0 to 2 s, constant to 6 s, falling linearly to -5 mm at 10 s, rising back to 0 at 12 s, then zero to 14 s.

EEP-20.alt: The extension graph with the positive region from 0 to 8 s shaded and labelled 30 mm s, and the negative triangle from 8 to 12 s shaded and labelled 10 mm s.

EEP-21-q.alt: Depth against time for the dive, with depth increasing downwards: 0 to 30 m in the first 3 min, 30 m until 18 min, rising to 5 m at 23 min, 5 m until 26 min, and the surface at 27 min.

EEP-21.alt: The dive profile with the area between the depth graph and the surface shaded and split into pieces of 45, 450, 87.5, 15 and 2.5 metre minutes.

EEP-22-q.alt: An amplifier box containing a 40 V alternating source in series with an 800 ohm resistor, connected to the 2000-turn primary coil of a transformer whose 200-turn secondary coil is connected to an 8 ohm loudspeaker.

EEP-25-q.alt: Circuit of a generator, an ideal diode, a 3.0 ohm resistor and a 6.0 V battery in series, with the diode pointing so that current flows from the generator's upper terminal into the battery's positive terminal; below it, a graph of the generator p.d. against time, a triangular wave between minus 12 V and plus 12 V with peaks at 10 ms and 30 ms and troughs at 0, 20 and 40 ms.

EEP-25.alt: Graph of charging current against time, zero except for triangular pulses from 7.5 to 12.5 ms and from 27.5 to 32.5 ms that peak at 2 A, each shaded and labelled as 5 mC.

EEP-26-q.alt: Velocity-time graph of two gliders: A starts at 0.8 m/s and B at 0; between 0 and about 16 ms A falls smoothly to -0.4 m/s and B rises smoothly to 0.4 m/s; the curves cross at 0.2 m/s at time t1, and the region between them from 0 to t1 is shaded.

EEP-27.alt: Two snapshots of a sine wave one flash apart: the dashed later wave has really moved 3.69 wavelengths forward, but its nearest crest is 0.31 wavelengths behind the original crest, so the eye sees a small backward step.

EE2-9-q.alt: Graph of y = f'(x): positive for x < -1, touching the x-axis at x = -1, positive again until crossing at x = 2, negative between 2 and 4, and positive after crossing at x = 4.

EE2-10-q.alt: Graph of y = f(x) for 0 to 6: an arch above the x-axis from 0 to 2 enclosing area 5, then a shallower trough below the axis from 2 to 6 enclosing area 3.

EE2-12.alt: The curve y = |x^2 - 2x| and the line y = x, meeting at x = 0, 1 and 3, with a small region of area 1/6 between 0 and 1 and a larger region of area 5/6 + 7/6 between 1 and 3 shaded.

EE2-13.alt: The sine curve and the line y = x/8 for x between about -9.6 and 9.6, crossing at seven marked points: the origin and three on each side, two of them just before x = 8.

EE2-15.alt: Four arches of y = f(x) on [-4,-2], [-2,0], [0,2] and [2,4], each twice as tall as the one to its left, shaded and labelled with areas 1/3, 2/3, 4/3 and 8/3.

EE2-18.alt: The licensed region: an octagon formed by the rectangle with corners A(0,0) and B(4,2), strips of width 2 on each side, and right-angled triangular corners, with vertices (-2,0), (-2,2), (0,4), (4,4), (6,2), (6,0), (4,-2) and (0,-2).

EE2-19.alt: The circle x^2 + y^2 = 25 and the wall 3x + 4y = 10, at distance 2 from the centre O, with the parallel tangent lines at distances 3 and 7 from the wall touching the circle at (3,4) and (-3,-4).

EE2-20.alt: The curve y = x^3 + x and its translate two units to the right, with the region R between them and between the lines y = 1 and y = 7 shaded, and a horizontal segment of length 2 across R.

EE2-25.alt: The curve y = x^2 and the line y = x/sqrt2 for 0 to 1, crossing at x = 1/sqrt2, with the gap regions on either side of the crossing shaded.

EE2-26.alt: The curve y = sqrt x for 0 to 4 between the chord y = x/2 and the parallel tangent y = x/2 + 1/2 (dashed), with the middle line y = x/2 + 1/4, which is 1/4 from the curve at x = 0, 1 and 4.

EF1-8.alt: A clock face with chords joining 12 to 4, 1 to 5 and 2 to 11; the small shaded triangle they form has angles of 30, 45 and 105 degrees.

EF1-13.alt: Vertical cross-section showing a large ball of radius 3 and the small ball of radius r touching on a table, with a right-angled triangle of sides 2 root 3, 3 minus r and hypotenuse 3 plus r joining their centres.

EF1-14.alt: Triangle OAB with P on AB, Q the midpoint of OP, and the line from A through Q meeting OB at R.

EF1-18.alt: The rug in its starting and finishing positions about the fixed corner O, with the swept region shaded: two triangles of area 6 and a quarter disc of radius 5 swept by the diagonal OC.

EF1-22.alt: View from above of the square floor: the wire appears as one diagonal and the pipe as the corner K, which is 3 root 2 from the diagonal.

EF1-25.alt: The parabola y equals x squared and the line y equals x minus 4, with the two squares of areas 18 and 50 that have two vertices on each.

EFP-2.alt: Free-body diagrams just after release: ball P has a 2.0 N weight and a 6.0 N spring pull, both downwards; ball Q has a 6.0 N spring pull upwards and a 6.0 N weight downwards.

EFP-3-q.alt: Upper oscilloscope screen, a 10 by 10 grid, showing a sine wave with a period of 4 divisions and an amplitude of 2 divisions. Below, six screens with the same grid: Graph A period 1 and amplitude 1 division; Graph B period 4 and amplitude 1; Graph C period 8 and amplitude 4; Graph D period 4 and amplitude 4; Graph E period 1 and amplitude 4; Graph F period 4 and amplitude 2.

EFP-4-q.alt: Temperature of the water against time over 216 s: a sawtooth that rises from 59.8 to 60.2 degrees Celsius in 24 s and falls back to 59.8 degrees in the next 48 s, repeated three times.

EFP-5-q.alt: A sealed vessel full of ice and water at 0 degrees Celsius, with an empty test tube projecting down into it from the top, and a narrow horizontal tube of area 5.0 square millimetres leading out of the side; water fills this tube up to a meniscus beside a scale.

EFP-9-q.alt: Graph of the frequency of the bat call against time: a straight line falling from 80 kHz at 0 ms to 30 kHz at 5.0 ms.

EFP-9.alt: Graph of the frequency heard against time: nothing is heard from 0 to 1.5 ms; then the heard frequency falls in a straight line from 20 kHz at 1.5 ms to zero at 3.5 ms, when the call is at 45 kHz, and rises in a straight line to 15 kHz at 5.0 ms.

EFP-10-q.alt: Two vertical metal plates, the left one positive and the right one negative, with a conducting ball hanging between them on an insulating thread; the plates are joined through an ammeter and a 4.0 kV supply.

EFP-11-q.alt: A truck facing right with a crate on its flat load bed, a distance d in front of the open rear edge.

EFP-11.alt: Velocity-time graphs: the truck rises from 0 to 12 m/s by 3 s and then stays at 12 m/s; the crate rises from 0 to 12 m/s by 4 s; the shaded triangle between them has area 6.0 m.

EFP-13-q.alt: A rigid bottle partly filled with water, sealed by a stopper through which an open vertical tube passes down into the water; its lower end T is below the water surface, with bubbles rising from it, and a tap near the bottom of the bottle is 20 cm below T.

EFP-14.alt: Detector reading against time over 72 hours: a sawtooth starting at the background of 50 counts per minute, jumping at each batch and decaying between batches; the peaks are 650, 800, 837.5 and about 847 counts per minute, approaching a dashed line at 850, and the troughs approach 250.

EFP-16-q.alt: Graph of current I against time t: I rises steadily from 0 to 3 A between 0 and 6 ms, stays at 3 A until 10 ms, falls steadily to zero at 12 ms and stays at zero until 16 ms, and the pattern repeats.

EFP-16.alt: Graph of induced p.d. against time over one 16 ms cycle: 2 V from 0 to 6 ms, zero from 6 to 10 ms, minus 6 V from 10 to 12 ms, zero from 12 to 16 ms, with the powers 0.50 W and 4.5 W marked.

EFP-17-q.alt: Power against time: rising linearly from 0 to 28.8 kW at 1 s, dropping to 24.0 kW and staying constant until 6 s, then dropping to 19.2 kW and falling linearly to zero at 7 s.

EFP-18-q.alt: A module of mass 280 kg with astronaut A of mass 45 kg at the left end and astronaut B of mass 75 kg at the right end, 4.0 m apart along a rail on its axis.

EFP-18.alt: Before and after the swap: the module has shifted 0.30 m in the direction A moved, with B now at the left end and A at the right end.

EFP-20-q.alt: Two copies of a circuit with a 12.0 V battery and resistors X and Y in series: in (a) the voltmeter is connected across X and reads 4.0 V; in (b) it is connected across Y and reads 6.0 V.

EFP-21-q.alt: A vertical lightning channel of height H rising from point G on flat ground, with microphones A and B on the ground on the same side of G, B further away than A.

EFP-21.alt: The same scene with distances in seconds of sound travel: the channel is 4, G to A is 3, A to B is 4.5, the top of the channel to A is 5 and to B is 8.5.

EFP-22-q.alt: Two drawings of the same cylinder, 1.0 m long: open end up, with a 30 cm air column at the closed bottom end below the piston; open end down, with a 50 cm air column at the closed top end above the piston.

EFP-22.alt: Free-body diagrams of the piston in three cases. Open end up at rest: air force pA upwards, atmospheric force p0 A and weight mg downwards. Open end down at rest: p0 A upwards, pA and mg downwards. Open end down in the lift accelerating upwards at half g: the same three forces, with an upward resultant of half mg.

EFP-23-q.alt: A single coil on an iron core with end terminals A and C and a tapping B; a 200 V supply is connected between A and B, with 500 turns between A and B and 100 turns between B and C, and a heater is connected between A and C.

EFP-23.alt: The booster circuit with currents marked: 12 A from the supply into B, 10 A up through section BC and the heater, and 2 A down through section AB back to A.

EFP-24-q.alt: A launcher fires a dart to the right towards a 160 g foam block on a frictionless air table, the block sliding left towards the launcher at 3.0 m/s.

EFP-26-q.alt: Three resistors R1, R2 and R3 in a chain along the bottom, with terminals T0, T1, T2 and T3 at the left end, the two joins and the right end; a meter of resistance 90 ohms is connected across the whole chain.

EFP-26.alt: General range connection: current I enters at a range terminal and splits into a shunt S carrying I minus 1.0 mA and a path of resistance R minus S in series with the 90 ohm meter carrying 1.0 mA, rejoining at T0.

EFP-27-q.alt: A vertical stack of three balls, X of 0.60 kg at the bottom, Y of 0.20 kg in the middle and Z of 0.10 kg on top, with the bottom of the stack 0.80 m above the floor.

EFP-27.alt: Three panels of velocities: after X bounces, X moves up at 4 while Y and Z move down at 4; after X hits Y, X is at rest and Y moves up at 8; after Y hits Z, X and Y are at rest and Z moves up at 12 metres per second.

EF2-4.alt: The first eight isosceles right-angled triangles of the spiral around O, of areas 64, 32, 16 and so on, filling the eight 45 degree angles at O, with the later tiny triangles lying inside them.

EF2-5.alt: The curve y = root x from 0 to 9 with the two trapezia under it shaded; the dividing point C is at x = 9/4, where the tangent is parallel to the chord AB.

EF2-11.alt: Plan view of the road with points A, B and C, 60 m and 20 m apart, joined to the foot T of the mast by lines of length 3h/2, 5h/4 and 4h/3, with the unknown angle theta at B.

EF2-12.alt: The parabola y = x squared and the circle with centre (-9, 6) that touches it at P(1, 1) and passes through Q(2, 4) and R(-4, 16), with triangle PQR shaded.

EF2-13.alt: The quartic curve with the straight line y = -8x - 21 through its two points I and J where the gradient is stationary, meeting the curve again at P and Q.

EF2-14.alt: The shortest route from A(-10, 0) to B(5, 5) round the pond: a tangent of length 5 root 3, an arc subtending 30 degrees, and a tangent of length 5.

EF2-15.alt: The curve y = x^3 - (4/3)x with the tangent at P, of gradient -1/2, meeting the curve again at Q, and the tangent at Q, of gradient 2, at right angles to it.

EF2-17.alt: Graph of the queue length Q = (t-3)^2(9-t) from t = 3 to t = 9, peaking at 32 when t = 7, with the area under it shaded.

EF2-18.alt: The cubic y = x^3 - 3x with a horizontal line y = k meeting it at a, b and c, and D marked as the distance from a to c.

EF2-19.alt: The band wiped by the vertical pantograph blade as its midpoint moves along a circular arc of radius 50 about O, with horizontal width 50 + 25 root 3.

EF2-20.alt: The ground profile with the light L at the top of the pole; the ray from L grazes the hill at T where x = 3/2 and reaches the ground at x = 3, and the unlit stretch between is highlighted.

EF2-21.alt: The shaded region R in the (p, q)-plane between the curves q = plus or minus 2(-p/3)^(3/2) for p from -3 to 0, meeting in a cusp at the origin.

EF2-23.alt: The parabola y = x^2, the line y = x - 2 and the point P(1/2, -3/2) on it, with the two tangents from P and the region between them and the parabola shaded.

EF2-25.alt: The curve y = 3x - x^3 and its reflection x = 3y - y^3 in the line y = x, crossing at nine marked points, three on the line y = x and six off it.

EF2-26.alt: The image region: the disc of radius 2 centred at (2, 0) with the disc of radius 2/3 centred at (10/3, 0) removed, both touching the line x = 4 at (4, 0).

EF2-27.alt: Graph of Bob's payment g(a): it dips to a minimum of -27/16 at a = 9/4, returns to 0 at a = 4 and then rises to 3 at a = 5; the dashed curve shows what would happen if b = root a were allowed beyond 2.
